newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest hogs called steady-up $0.50 - trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest hogs called steady-up $0.50 - trade.

text.p: U.S. Midwest cash hog prices were called steady to $0.50 per cwt higher Thursday as meat packers appear to be increasing slaughter rates in reaction to higher cash pork prices, livestock dealers said.
"I think whoever was cut back is not cut back anymore," said a Minnesota dealer.
USDA estimated Wednesday's hog slaughter at 370,000 head versus 357,000 a week ago and 366,000 a year ago.
Also, dealers said some packers may resume Saturday slaughter operations. A dealer said a local packer, which had not operated Saturday for some time, was to run a shift then.
Evidence of rising pork prices was apparent in USDA's pork cutout values, which rose to $80.85 per cwt Tuesday for U.S. Grade 1 carcasses from $76.54 on Nov 13.

Interior Iowa sources said four to five inches of snow in northern areas may slow hog marketings Thursday. Also, he said a few areas had snow mixed with ice which may slicken roads and impede transportation.
